|total owned-entry runs |6,561 |

Those runs checked 14,537 actual modeled transitions, 21,098 inclusive prefix
states and 7,605 raw-pop observations. Four additional actual caller scenarios
check both sentinel clocks, allocation beyond the first handoff and fabricated
later success. Every input and result is retained in ordinary UTF-8 files;
full local traces plus the explicitly checked unchanged caller/protected data
reconstruct each complete prefix configuration. No compressed/opaque blob is
needed. Named cases and caller traces are also saved separately for inspection.

This finite diagnostic evidence supports the listed concrete cases. It does
not establish universal Lean theorems, a compiled finite program, a package
instance, compiler success or a formal audit. All public executions, generalized
endpoints, failure source-cost decompositions, exact ranks, first-handoff/source
equivalences, arbitrary-family preservation, all-N sharpness, exact debt/mass,
finite package data and actual timed caller compositions above remain to be
implemented and checked after the source-scope release.

## 10. Complete remaining integration boundary

This parser recognizes one syntactic move prefix and preserves its suffix. It
does not validate the represented tree, perform a rotation, parse the entire
certificate, compare target trees, or produce a Boolean verifier answer.
The existing planned front-end and fixed-width predecessor must precede it on
each nonempty certificate. Zero fuel must preserve the complete certificate
without entering these blocks. Empty certificate handling belongs to the
surrounding stream logic; the parser itself correctly rejects empty raw.

Its live success direction and actual forward Branch path must next feed the
represented rotation operation. Structural equality, repeated streaming,
Boolean cleanup/termination, quantitative TM2-to-TM1 simulation and formal NP
correspondence remain mandatory. Any reuse of the existing two emptied Bool
stacks for these Branch stacks needs explicit alphabet equivalences, complete
physical/register/label bijections, installed-program transport and handoff
equations. No hidden list conversion, free transfer, accepted integrated cell
count or global verifier theorem follows from the local parser proposal.

## 2. Mathematical notation and finite runtime carriers

All lists are written with their physical top at the left. `0` is `emptyTag`
and `1` is `nodeTag`; other elements of `Tag` are literal foreign symbols for
the tree scanner. A tree in the machine correspondence is `BinaryTree Unit`.
For readable mathematics, `node A B` suppresses the actual Unit node payload.
Write `code t` for `treeCode t`. Thus `code nil = [0]` and
`code (node A B) = [1] ++ code A ++ code B`.

Use these five local physical stacks and the arbitrary protected family:

| Local stack | Alphabet | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `Tag` | Current whole represented tree prefix, with any untouched suffix |
| `saved` | `Tag` | Reversed literal context prefix during navigation |
| `scratch` | `Tag` | Reversed scanned subtree prefix during the root rewrite |
| `pending` | `Unit` | Outstanding tree slots |
| `path` | `Branch` | Actual remaining root-to-focus path |

Let `StackId K = LocalStack ⊕ K`; protected index `k` has alphabet `Γ k`.
Use `saved` or `prefixRev` as an identifier, since bare `prefix` is reserved in
Lean. A proof-side `LocalData` record contains exactly the five actual lists.

The owned phase type has exactly sixteen values:

| Constructor family | Values |
|---|---:|
| `seek d` | 2 |
| `scanPrefix d` | 2 |
| `start d` | 2 |
| `scanScratch d` | 2 |
| `checkRight` | 1 |
| `restoreScratch mode` | 4 |
| `dropPending` | 1 |
| `restorePrefix result` | 2 |

The four modes are `successLeft`, `successRight`, `failureLeft`, and
`failureRight`. Use a fresh two-valued result type `success | failure`; the
MoveParser result type has three values and is not this result type.
Set `External Λ = Result ⊕ Λ` and `Label Λ = Phase ⊕ External Λ`.
`Owned` holds exactly at `some (phaseLabel phase)`. Results and arbitrary caller
labels are live nonowned labels. The halted label `none` is also nonowned.

The temporary state is
`Option Branch × (Option Tag × Option Unit)`, with `3 · 17 · 2 = 102` values.
The full register is that temporary state paired with a caller register `R`.
`reset` replaces the three temporary fields by `none` and leaves `R` literal.
Individual pop/peek updates change only their named temporary field. Every
owned goto is preceded by reset. Branch tests and pushed values inspect only
these finite fields or fixed constants. No callback may inspect a list,
unbounded natural, source evaluator, tree, path length, rank, or potential.

Structural statements need only the actual index decidability required by TM2
updates, not finiteness of the protected family, caller labels, or caller
register. The finite machine package additionally assumes finite `K`, `Λ`, `R`,
and every `Γ k`. Its exact dimensions are:

\[
|StackId\ K|=5+|K|,\quad |Label\ \Lambda|=18+|\Lambda|,
\quad |Registers\ R|=102|R|.
\]

The subtype of owned labels has cardinality sixteen even for infinite `Λ`.
A fixture with two protected stacks, one arbitrary external label, and Boolean
caller register has dimensions `7 / 19 / 204`. Every actual local alphabet and
every supplied protected alphabet must have its finite instance exhibited.

## 3. Complete fixed finite program

`program caller` maps an owned phase to its fixed block and a nonowned live
label to the supplied caller block. `jump q` means a `load reset` followed by
a constant `goto q`. `restoreObserved q` means a finite test of whether the
current Tag observation is present, then a push of that literal Tag if present,
then `q`. A total fallback value in the push callback is permitted only under
that present-observation guard; it must never replace a foreign observed Tag.

Each row below is **one actual TM2 activation**, not one transition for each
listed primitive. It fixes the same program as the retained finite AST.

| Owned phase and observation | Actual primitives and destination |
|---|---|
| `seek d`, path empty | Pop path into the branch field; on `none`, jump to `start d`. Do not inspect source. |
| `seek d`, path head `b`, source node | Pop path, then source. Push the observed node to saved. For `b = left`, jump to `seek d`. For `b = right`, push one pending Unit and jump to `scanPrefix d`. |
| `seek d`, path head present, source nonnode/EOF | Restore the present source observation literally, then jump to `dropPending`. The path head just popped remains consumed. |
| `scanPrefix d`, source node | Pop source, push node to saved, push one pending Unit, and jump to the same phase. |
| `scanPrefix d`, source empty-tree Tag | Pop source, push that Tag to saved, pop pending into the Unit field, **peek pending into that same field**, then repeat if the peek is present, otherwise jump to `seek d`. |
| `scanPrefix d`, source foreign/EOF | Restore the present foreign Tag before jumping to `dropPending`. |
| `start left`, source node | Pop source, push one pending Unit, and jump to `scanScratch left`. |
| `start left`, source nonnode/EOF | Restore the present observation and jump to `dropPending`. |
| `start right`, first and second source observations both node | Perform both pops in this block, push one pending Unit, and jump to `scanScratch right`. |
| `start right`, first observation nonnode/EOF | Restore that present observation and jump to `dropPending`. |
| `start right`, first node but second nonnode/EOF | Restore the second observation if present, then push the first node, then jump to `dropPending`, all in this block. |
| `scanScratch d`, source node | Pop source, push node to scratch, push one pending Unit, and repeat. |
| `scanScratch d`, source empty-tree Tag, pending remains after pop | Push the Tag to scratch, pop and then peek pending, and repeat. |
| `scanScratch left`, source empty-tree Tag, pending empty after pop | Push the Tag to scratch, pop and peek pending, and jump to `checkRight`. |
| `scanScratch right`, source empty-tree Tag, pending empty after pop | Push the Tag to scratch, pop and peek pending, **push node to source in this same activation**, and jump to `restoreScratch successRight`. |
| `scanScratch d`, source foreign/EOF | Restore the present foreign Tag and jump to the direction's failure restoration mode. |
| `checkRight`, source node | Pop that node and jump to `restoreScratch successLeft`. |
| `checkRight`, source nonnode/EOF | Restore the present observation and jump to `restoreScratch failureLeft`. |
| `restoreScratch mode`, scratch nonempty | Pop a Tag, push that literal Tag to source, and repeat the same mode. |
| `restoreScratch successLeft`, scratch empty | The empty probe pushes two nodes, then jumps to `restorePrefix success`. |
| `restoreScratch successRight`, scratch empty | The empty probe pushes one node, then jumps to `restorePrefix success`. |
| `restoreScratch failureLeft`, scratch empty | The empty probe pushes one node, then jumps to `dropPending`. |
| `restoreScratch failureRight`, scratch empty | The empty probe pushes two nodes, then jumps to `dropPending`. |
| `dropPending`, pending nonempty | Pop one Unit and repeat. |
| `dropPending`, pending empty | The empty probe jumps to `restorePrefix failure`. |
| `restorePrefix r`, saved nonempty | Pop a Tag, push it literally to source, and repeat. |
| `restorePrefix r`, saved empty | The empty probe jumps to the live result `r`. |

The branch field must survive the source pop in `seek`. The scanner's decision
uses the actual **peek after pop**, not stale Unit state or the just-popped
Unit. Restoration occurs before reset. No owned block halts.

The retained AST's longest constructor path is ten primitives; the fresh
finite support calculation reproduced that syntactic number. The future Lean
blocks should admit the same fixed syntactic bound if it is useful to expose
it. This is separate from the TM2 activation count, and does not supply a
quantitative TM2-to-TM1 theorem.

## 4. Arbitrary dirty-state one-step semantics and total evaluation

Define a proof-only control type `Control = Phase ⊕ Result` and a **nonrecursive**
function `advance : Phase → LocalData → Control × LocalData` by the exact head,
empty, and branch cases above. It neither calls the program nor evaluates a
source tree. Conversely, no runtime callback calls `advance`.

Use a configuration constructor with label argument `Option (Label Λ)`, the
complete register, `LocalData`, and the protected context. Its extensionality
and eta lemmas expose every actual stack. The first universal theorem must
identify the actual complete successor:

\[
step\ caller\bigl(cfg\ (some\ (phaseLabel\ q))\ regs\ D\ ctx\bigr)
= some\bigl(cfg\ (some\ (controlLabel\ q'))\ (reset\ regs)\ D'\ ctx\bigr),
\qquad (q',D')=advance(q,D).
\]

Quantify over every owned phase, all five arbitrary finite lists, all 102 stale
temporary values, arbitrary caller register, protected context, and caller
program. This is equality of label, complete register, and every dependent
physical stack. Export the meaningful branch equations as usable one-step
lemmas, including EOF versus foreign restoration and the right-start second-pop
failure. A theorem only about a projected return value is insufficient.

### A natural countdown valid on every dirty state

Let `L,F,S,H,P` be the old lengths of source, saved, scratch, pending, and path,
and let `W = 3L + F + S + H + P`. Define the proof-only countdown `T`:

| Control | `T` |
|---|---:|
| `seek`, `scanPrefix`, `scanScratch` | `W + 5` |
| `start` | `W + 4` |
| `checkRight` | `W + 6` |
| `restoreScratch` success mode | `S + F + 2` |
| `restoreScratch` failure mode | `S + H + F + 3` |
| `dropPending` | `H + F + 2` |
| `restorePrefix` | `F + 1` |
| Result or nonowned label | `0` |

This is a termination majorant, not the exact clock. With
`e = min(H,1)`, the exact arithmetic differences are:

| Actual branch | `T(before) − T(after)` |
|---|---:|
| Seek with empty path | `1` |
| Seek node, left / right | `3 / 2` |
| Seek failed source observation | `3L + S + P + 3` |
| Prefix scan node | `1` |
| Prefix scan empty-tree Tag, continuing | `3` |
| Prefix scan empty-tree Tag, finishing | `2 + e` |
| Prefix scan foreign/EOF | `3L + S + P + 3` |
| Start left node / right two nodes | `1 / 4` |
| Any failed start | `3L + S + P + 2` |
| Scratch scan node | `1` |
| Scratch scan empty-tree Tag, continuing | `3` |
| Scratch scan final empty-tree Tag, left | `1 + e` |
| Scratch scan final empty-tree Tag, right | `3L + H + P + 2` |
| Scratch scan foreign/EOF | `3L + P + 2` |
| Check-right node | `3L + H + P + 4` |
| Check-right failed observation | `3L + P + 3` |
| Every scratch transfer or empty marker probe | `1` |
| Every pending drop or empty probe | `1` |
| Every saved transfer or final probe | `1` |

For the continuing empty-Tag cases, `H ≥ 2`; for the finishing cases, `H ≤ 1`.
The table covers `H = 0`. The right-final scratch row includes the node pushed
in that same block. All entries are positive in the branch in which they occur.
Prove `T(next) + 1 ≤ T(current)` by the actual successor cases and elementary
natural arithmetic, with no cleanliness assumption.

Define total proof-only `evaluate` by well-founded recursion on `T`. At a
result, it returns that result, the literal data, and zero steps. At an owned
phase, it evaluates `advance` and adds one to the successor's step count. Let
`Q(q,D)` be that count. Required equations and bounds are:

\[
Q(result,D)=0,\quad
Q(q,D)=1+Q(advance(q,D)),\quad
0<Q(q,D)\text{ for owned }q,\quad Q(q,D)\le T(q,D).
\]

The endpoint and exact-iteration theorem follow from this recursion and the
actual one-step theorem. It must give every dirty phase's literal endpoint,
not infer clean scratch/pending merely from the phase name. The evaluator is
not a trace-length definition taken from a completed experiment.

For clean entry at `seek d` with source `w`, path `p`, and other local stores
empty, define `runSteps d w p = Q(seek d, w, [], [], [], p)`. Then retain both
the derived bound and the intended conservative public bound:

\[
runSteps(d,w,p)\le 3|w|+|p|+5\le 4|w|+|p|+12.
\]

Do not rename either upper bound as exact time. The exact clock is `Q`.

## 5. Generalized physical transfers and scanner lemmas

These lemmas quantify over arbitrary old accumulators, raw suffixes, remaining
path, stale registers, caller register, and protected context. They are actual
iterations under `program caller`. Positive iterations reset the finite
temporaries; a zero-length iteration preserves the original entire register.

### Transfers and empty probes

From scratch `accepted ++ rest`, exactly `|accepted|` scratch-transfer steps
leave scratch `rest` and source `accepted.reverse ++ oldSource`. Saved, pending,
path, caller register, and context are literal. The next empty probe is charged
only when `rest = []`; it physically inserts the mode's marker word.

Let `M(successLeft) = M(failureRight) = [1,1]` and
`M(successRight) = M(failureLeft) = [1]`. With initial source `w`, saved `f`,
scratch `s`, pending `h`, and path `p`, full generalized restoration has:

| Entry | Exact first-result time | Literal endpoint |
|---|---:|---|
| Successful `restoreScratch mode` | `|s| + |f| + 2` | Success; source `f.reverse ++ M(mode) ++ s.reverse ++ w`; saved/scratch empty; **pending remains `h`**; path `p` |
| Failed `restoreScratch mode` | `|s| + |h| + |f| + 3` | Failure; same source formula; saved/scratch/pending empty; path `p` |
| `dropPending` | `|h| + |f| + 2` | Failure; source `f.reverse ++ w`; saved/pending empty; **scratch remains `s`**; path `p` |
| `restorePrefix r` | `|f| + 1` | Result `r`; source `f.reverse ++ w`; saved empty; scratch `s`, pending `h`, and path `p` unchanged |

Also export split-prefix transfer/drop lemmas. Their step counts do not include
an unperformed empty probe. The positive-time final register is `reset regs`.

### A raw continuing-scan relation

Define `Continues w h k` independently of machine execution, where `h,k` are
pending counts. Empty word leaves the count unchanged. A node is accepted and
increases the count by one. An empty-tree Tag is a **continuing** symbol only
when the current count is at least two, and decreases it by one. No foreign
Tag belongs to this relation. A recursive formulation processes each head
before the relation for the tail.

For `Continues w h k`, starting source `w ++ rest`, pending `replicate h ()`,
and accumulator `a`, exactly `|w|` steps remain in the same scanner with source
`rest`, accumulator `w.reverse ++ a`, and pending `replicate k ()`. The
accumulator is saved for `scanPrefix` and scratch for `scanScratch`. Other
stores are unchanged, subject to the exact register reset rule above.

If the next symbol is an empty-tree Tag and `k ≤ 1`, one more step ends that
scanner and leaves pending empty. Prefix scanning goes to seek; left scratch
scanning goes to check-right; right scratch scanning goes to successful
restoration and prepends its actual node to source. Include `k = 0`, rather
than inserting an implicit one-slot precondition.

For a continuing `w` followed by `blocked`, where `blocked` is empty or starts
with a Tag unequal to both `0` and `1`, let `k` be the count after `w`:

| Starting scanner | Exact time through full failure cleanup | Source at first failure |
|---|---:|---|
| Prefix, old saved `f` | `2|w| + k + |f| + 3` | `f.reverse ++ w ++ blocked`; old scratch remains literal |
| Scratch in direction `d`, old scratch `s`, saved `f` | `2|w| + k + |s| + |f| + 4` | `f.reverse ++ failedMarkers(d) ++ s.reverse ++ w ++ blocked` |

Here `failedMarkers(left)=[1]` and `failedMarkers(right)=[1,1]`. These formulas
require `Continues`; a bare numeric slot count does not justify them. The
foreign blocking Tag is not lost during the failing activation.

### Represented subtree and forest scans

The stronger reusable represented scanner theorem begins with source
`code t ++ z`, pending `() :: outerPending`, and arbitrary old accumulator `a`.
After exactly `|code t|` actual steps, the accumulator is
`(code t).reverse ++ a`, and pending is `outerPending`.

If `outerPending` is nonempty, the same scanner remains owned with source `z`.
If it is empty, the scanner exits as described above; the right scratch case
has source `1 :: z`, because the marker push has already happened. Every
unvisited suffix Tag and every other store remains literal. Prove this by
induction on the actual Unit tree, carrying arbitrary old accumulators. A
forest version is composition of these actual scans.

The initial slot premise matters. On scanner source `[1,0,0]`, empty pending
exits after two Tags and leaves source `[0]`; one pending Unit consumes all
three Tags. A claim that every arbitrary dirty scanner consumes one represented
tree is false.

## 6. All-raw cleanup and exact rollback

For a clean `seek d` entry with arbitrary raw `w` and arbitrary physical path
`p`, total evaluation must produce a live result and endpoint data
`(w', [], [], [], p')`, reset temporaries, unchanged caller register, and
unchanged protected context. The physical remaining path is a suffix of `p`.

Required clean-entry conclusions are:

* Failure restores **the literal whole original word**: `w' = w`, including
  every foreign Tag and arbitrary suffix. The consumed path prefix is not
  restored.
* Success leaves `p' = []` and preserves the whole source length: `|w'|=|w|`.
  It empties saved, scratch, and pending.
* The exact endpoint time is `runSteps d w p`, with all earlier labels owned.

Useful proof invariants relate the original source to actual stores:

| Stage before cleanup | Literal decomposition |
|---|---|
| Navigation | `original = saved.reverse ++ source`, with scratch empty |
| Left root scratch scan | `original = saved.reverse ++ [1] ++ scratch.reverse ++ source` |
| Right root scratch scan | `original = saved.reverse ++ [1,1] ++ scratch.reverse ++ source` |

Refine these at the left check and successful rewrite transitions as needed.
Failure restoration must account for the observed Tag restored **in the same
block**, then the exact missing root markers, then saved restoration. For
successful clean runs, tag-plus-debt conservation below yields length
preservation once the actual clean endpoint has been proved.

Raw success alone does not imply a valid whole tree. A clean left root entry
on `[1,0,1,15]` succeeds in seven activations with `[1,1,0,15]`; neither is a
whole tree code. The represented theorem below therefore assumes an upstream
represented source. It must not derive validity from a success label.

A useful additional exact raw-root characterization is:

| Direction | Raw success condition | Output and exact clock |
|---|---|---|
| Left, empty path | `w = [1] ++ code A ++ [1] ++ z` for some Unit tree `A` and raw `z` | `[1,1] ++ code A ++ z`, time `2|code A|+5` |
| Right, empty path | `w = [1,1] ++ code A ++ z` for some Unit tree `A` and raw `z` | `[1] ++ code A ++ [1] ++ z`, time `2|code A|+4` |

Prove both directions from the actual scanner behavior and tree-prefix
recognition, not from a claim that `z` is a tree. These characterizations are
root-entry statements; arbitrary dirty-phase results remain those of the full
evaluator.

Retain the exact raw path-stop family as a separate clock discriminator. On
source `replicate n nodeTag` and path `replicate (n+k) left`, with `k≥1`, either
direction fails in `2n+3`, restores the original raw source, and leaves
`replicate (k−1) left`. Exactly one failing path head was popped after the `n`
successful descents. With path `replicate n left`, root execution at EOF instead
fails in `2n+4` and leaves empty path. These families witness that an unvisited
path tail does not contribute work merely because it was present initially.

## 7. Represented cursor, physical path, and source semantics

### Literal cursor representation

Use nearest-focus-first frames `cameLeft rightSibling` and
`cameRight leftSibling`. Define `plug [] focus = focus`; for a nonempty frame
list, rebuild the immediate parent and continue through the outer frames.
Define context prefix `pre` and suffix `suf` by:

\[
\begin{aligned}
pre([])&=[] & suf([])&=[]\\
pre(cameLeft\ r::fs)&=pre(fs)++[1]
& suf(cameLeft\ r::fs)&=code(r)++suf(fs)\\
pre(cameRight\ l::fs)&=pre(fs)++[1]++code(l)
& suf(cameRight\ l::fs)&=suf(fs).
\end{aligned}
\]

Prove the literal identity

\[
code(plug\ fs\ focus)=pre(fs)++code(focus)++suf(fs).
\]

An independent cursor relation follows the actual Branch heads through nodes
until the path is exhausted or the focus is nil. Let `j` count successful
ancestor descents, and `m = |pre fs|`. Starting with source `code s ++ z`, old
saved `f`, empty scratch/pending, and path `p`, exactly `m` navigation activations
reach seek with:

* source `code focus ++ suf fs ++ z`;
* saved `(pre fs).reverse ++ f`;
* scratch and pending empty;
* the actual unvisited path;
* the original full register if `m=0`, reset temporaries otherwise;
* unchanged caller register and protected context.

A left descent consumes one node Tag and costs one activation. A right descent
costs `1+|code leftSibling|`, using the represented prefix-scanner lemma; saved
grows by the reverse of that same literal prefix. Thus `m` is not merely the
path depth. This navigation theorem stops before the final path-empty probe or
the failed source observation at a nil focus.

### Remaining physical path

Define the residual path function independently of direction:

\[
\begin{aligned}
res([],s)&=[]\\
res(b::p,nil)&=p\\
res(left::p,node\ l\ r)&=res(p,l)\\
res(right::p,node\ l\ r)&=res(p,r).
\end{aligned}
\]

At a missing node with nonempty path, the failing head is actually popped but
the tail is not traversed. At exhausted path, the path remains empty. This is
the physical path result in both success and failure theorems.

### Exact represented machine clock

Define a proof-only `representedClock d p s` by these exhaustive equations:

| Actual tree/path case | Machine clock |
|---|---:|
| Empty path, nil tree, either direction | `4` |
| Empty path, left at `node A nil` | `2|code A|+6` |
| Empty path, left at `node A (node B C)` | `2|code A|+5` |
| Empty path, right at `node nil C` | `4` |
| Empty path, right at `node (node A B) C` | `2|code A|+4` |
| Nonempty path, nil tree | `3` |
| `left :: p`, node `l r` | `representedClock d p l + 2` |
| `right :: p`, node `l r` | `representedClock d p r + 2(1+|code l|)` |

The principal represented theorem is strengthened to **arbitrary old saved
word `f` and arbitrary raw suffix `z`**. Start at seek with source `code s ++ z`,
saved `f`, scratch/pending empty, and path `p`. Let
`actual = applyMoveRun ⟨d,p⟩ s`, using the real direction-first `RotationMove`
constructor. At exactly `representedClock d p s + |f|` activations:

| Actual source result | Live result | Literal source |
|---|---|---|
| `actual.1 = some t` | Success | `f.reverse ++ code t ++ z` |
| `actual.1 = none` | Failure | `f.reverse ++ code s ++ z` |

In both rows, saved/scratch/pending are empty, path is `res p s`, the finite
temporaries are reset, and caller/context are unchanged. No suffix validity
premise is allowed. The theorem must also identify the exact evaluator clock
`Q = representedClock + |f|` and establish ownership at every strict earlier
prefix. On success, path is empty.

The extra `|f|` is essential to the induction. A left step spends one and grows
saved by one; a right step spends and saves `1+|code l|`. Applying the child
theorem with that enlarged saved word yields precisely the two recurrence
equations. An endpoint equality at some eventual time alone cannot identify
the first-return clock under arbitrary callers.

### Exact source-event clock and its relation to machine time

The actual source implementation charges root rotation success four events,
failure two; an empty `applyAtRun` path adds one. Each successfully reconstructed
ancestor adds three, each failed ancestor adds two. Nonempty path at nil costs
two immediately. Prove the source result and source cost together using these
actual recursive equations.

For the stopped cursor above, with scanned subtree code length `a` where
applicable, the exact comparison is:

| Stopped cursor outcome | `(applyMoveRun ⟨d,p⟩ s).2` | `representedClock d p s` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Left success | `3j+5` | `2m+2a+5` |
| Right success | `3j+5` | `2m+2a+4` |
| Nonempty path reaches nil | `2j+2` | `2m+3` |
| Exhausted path reaches nil | `2j+3` | `2m+4` |
| Right rotation has nil left child | `2j+3` | `2m+4` |
| Left rotation has nil right child | `2j+3` | `2m+2a+6` |

Here `a` is the actually scanned `A` subtree, not the full current tree. On
success `j=|p|`. On a missing-node failure, `j` excludes the final failed path
pop. Adding old saved `f` changes the machine clock by `|f|` and leaves the
source-event clock unchanged. Raw suffix `z` changes neither exact represented
clock. These are different cost models; neither is a relabeling of the other.

For the same tree `node rightTwo rightTwo`, left rotation at `[L]` and `[R]`
both have source work 8, but machine clocks 9 and 19 respectively. The right
route physically scans and restores the left sibling code. Include this
same-tree discriminator so a path-length formula cannot replace the actual
context-prefix length.

Connect success to actual `applyMoveRun_value`, node preservation via
`applyMoveRun_numNodes`, and source success cost `3|p|+5`. Use actual
`treeCode_length = 2*numNodes+1` for represented output lengths. The existing
`parseTreeRun_prefix_injective s t rest suffix` consumes the equality
`code s ++ rest = code t ++ suffix` and gives both `s=t` and `rest=suffix`.
For dirty old saved `f`, first cancel the common prefix `f.reverse`; do not
silently feed the uncancelled equality to that API.

The source inverse theorem concerns the opposite direction at the **same
position**. A successful machine run consumes that physical position, so a
second machine invocation needs an actual path reinstallation before that
source inverse theorem applies.

## 8. All inclusive prefixes, exact first handoff, and caller boundaries

Lift `Q` to actual configurations as `remainingSteps c`, using local data at an
owned phase and zero at every nonowned label or halted configuration. Prove:

* positive remaining steps iff owned label;
* actual progress from every owned configuration;
* exact decrease by one on every owned step;
* all protected-stack and caller-register preservation for the owned step relation;
* finite temporary reset after every such step.

Use the existing FixedWidth `ranked_prefix` theorem, whose progress premise is
`rank c = rank d + 1`, to obtain one shared configuration for each
`n ≤ remainingSteps start`. That same witness must satisfy the actual iteration
equation, rank `remainingSteps start − n`, and an owned-step reflexive/transitive
path. Carry register, context, tag, potential, and space statements for this
same actual reached configuration.

For an **owned start**, all `n<Q` prefixes are present and owned, and `n=Q`
is the exact live result prescribed by evaluation. The result caller has not
executed. Define first handoff with both a nonowned endpoint and ownership at
every strict earlier prefix; prove its time and endpoint are unique. Do not
assert that every later nonowned observation is the first result.

For a nonowned start, `Q=0` gives only the identity prefix. It does not turn an
arbitrary caller or halted state into a live local result. At `n=0`, the entire
original register is unchanged, including stale temporary fields. At positive
prefix times through the owned run, all three temporary fields are reset.
Caller-register preservation is unconditional throughout those prefixes.

Prove one-step independence from arbitrary caller bodies at owned labels and

program whose installed statements agree with these blocks on owned labels.
Its actual prefix is identical through first handoff. No agreement, frame, or

Required caller discriminators include these actual same-program runs:

|---|---|

| Nil source, path `[L,R,L]`, same caller | Live failure at 3 with remaining path `[R,L]`; present halted configuration at 4; outer `none` at 5 |
| Caller allocating protected cells | May exceed the owned-prefix cell bound immediately after handoff |
| Caller that jumps to the opposite result | An eventual success/failure observation is not necessarily the first source-connected result |

Also distinguish Tag13 and Tag14 sentinel callers: their actual prefixes agree
through `Q` and differ at `Q+1`. Exercise the separate external-label

5, external push-Tag13/halt at 6, and outer `none` at 7. Each continuation is an

For inverse reentry, let `one = node nil nil`,
`rightTwo = node nil one`, `leftTwo = node one nil`, and
`leftContext = node rightTwo nil`. Left rotation at `[L]` returns
`node leftTwo nil` in 9. A plain result caller that jumps to right seek uses

## 9. Actual physical cells, marker debt, and potential

With finite protected index type `K`, define the public space measure as the
actual dependent sum:

\[
stackCells(c)=\sum_{k:StackId\ K}|c.stk(k)|.
\]

Let `U = ∑ k:K, |ctx k|`. Prove from the actual configuration definition that
`stackCells(cfg …) = L+F+S+H+P+U`. This includes every local and protected stack.
It is a physical stack-cell measure, not a claim about bits, host evaluator
memory, or TM1 tape cells. The finite register is separate fixed control.

Let `tagCells=L+F+S`. Define marker debt by control:

| Control | Debt |
|---|---:|
| `scanScratch left`, `checkRight`, `restoreScratch successRight`, `restoreScratch failureLeft` | `1` |
| `scanScratch right`, `restoreScratch successLeft`, `restoreScratch failureRight` | `2` |
| Every other phase, result, caller, or halted label | `0` |

Every owned step must conserve `tagCells + debt` **exactly**. This includes
two-marker insertions in a single empty-probe block and the right scanner's
same-activation source push. Dirty scratch and saved Tags are counted literally.

Credit is `L` at seek, prefix scan, start, scratch scan, and check-right, and
zero elsewhere. Define

\[
\Phi(c)=stackCells(c)+debt(c.l)+credit(c).
\]

Prove nonincrease at every owned step. Local potential algebra does not need
finite `K`; the physical finite sum adds the unchanged protected total. With
old source length `L` and `e=min(H,1)`, the exact decreases are:

| Actual branch | `Phi(before) − Phi(after)` |
|---|---:|
| Seek with empty path | `0` |
| Seek node, left / right | `2 / 1` |
| Seek failed source observation | `L+1` |
| Prefix or scratch scan node | `0` |
| Prefix scan empty-tree Tag | `e+1` |
| Prefix scan foreign/EOF | `L` |
| Start left node / right two nodes | `0 / 1` |
| Any failed start | `L` |
| Scratch continuing empty-tree Tag | `2` |
| Scratch final empty-tree Tag, left / right | `e+1 / L+e` |
| Scratch scan foreign/EOF | `L` |
| Either check-right outcome | `L` |
| Scratch transfer or empty marker insertion | `0` |
| Pending nonempty drop / empty probe | `1 / 0` |
| Saved transfer or final probe | `0` |

The countdown in Section 4 strictly decreases; this physical potential often
stays equal. They serve different purposes and must not be conflated.

Every inclusive prefix from an arbitrary dirty owned start satisfies
`stackCells reached ≤ Phi start`, retaining its actual old stores, debt,
credit, and protected total. For a clean seek entry with source `w` and path
`p`, initial potential is exactly `2|w|+|p|+U`, giving:

\[
n\le runSteps(d,w,p)\Longrightarrow
stackCells(reached_n)\le 2|w|+|p|+U.
\]

Keep the endpoint included and identify the reached configuration by its actual
iteration equation. There is no extension past handoff to arbitrary callers.

### Exact families and necessary dirty-state terms

For clean left entry on `replicate N nodeTag`, path empty, prove exact first
failure time `3N+4`. At time `2N+2`, the **actual** configuration is
`dropPending`, source is the original `N` nodes, pending has `N` Units, saved,
scratch, and path are empty, registers are reset, and context is unchanged.
Its cells are `2N+U`, attaining the clean space bound, and remaining rank is
`N+2`, so it is strictly before handoff. This includes `N=0`: drop at 2,
failure at 4. State exact family time without claiming it attains the coarser
public time bound.

For clean right entry on `replicate (m+2) nodeTag`, path empty, prove exact
failure time `3m+7`. At time `2m+4`, source is restored, pending has `m+1` Units,
and the same other stores are empty. Its cells are `2m+3+U`, with remaining
rank `m+3`. This right family is one cell below the clean entry budget and is
not mislabeled as attaining that budget.

The case plan must separate necessary hypotheses:

* Empty `restoreScratch successLeft` inserts two source nodes in one step;
  its initial debt two is needed for the dirty bound.
* Prefix scan on source `[1]` with empty pending grows a pending cell; source
  credit is needed in addition to Tag conservation.
* At clean represented source `code rightTwo`, a left root rotation takes 7.
  Giving seek one old pending Unit instead makes it scan too far and fail in

* A dirty successful scratch restoration preserves pending, and dirty pending
  cleanup preserves scratch. Neither cleanup label licenses erasing that data.

left-Branch and Tag 14 are added to the imported model's in-memory constant
interpretation; Tag 13 was already supported. The archived model file is unchanged.

These calculations are ordinary Python evidence, not a verified TM2 interpreter,
kernel proof, universal enumeration of words, or evidence of whole-verifier
acceptance. Every future Lean execution case must consume the actual new
producer's finite program, configuration, step/iterate and public contracts.

## 1. Notation, concrete fixtures and finite carriers

Use five real local stores, in this order:

`D = (X,F,S,H,P)` = source Tags, saved reversed prefix Tags, reversed scratch
Tags, pending Units, and path Branches. The retained Python model calls F
`prefix`; use a valid Lean identifier such as `saved` or `prefixRev`. Lists are
written top-first. `L`/`R` inside a path denote Branch values, not rotation
directions. A move is direction first, position second in the actual
`RotationMove` record. Tag 0 is `emptyTag`; Tag 1 is `nodeTag`; every Tag 2–15 is a
foreign tree observation but remains a legitimate physical Tag.

The default concrete protected family has two distinct stacks: Tag word
`[15,2,7,10,3]` and Unit word `[(),()]`, so U=7. The Tag word is intentionally
nonpalindromic. Principal statements quantify over arbitrary dependent K/Γ,
protected contents and caller register R. Concrete clients use K=Fin2, external
labels Unit and caller register Bool, and retain both true and false cases.
The ordinary stale temporary tuple is `(some R,some 15,some ())`; additionally
exercise all 102 finite temporary values. At step 0 retain the actual original
tuple; every positive owned step must reset all three fields.

| Actual carrier | Required cardinality |
|---|---:|
| Local stack identifiers | 5 |
| Owned phase labels | 16 |
| Temporary tuple `Option Branch × (Option Tag × Option Unit)` | 3×17×2=102 |
| Full stack family | 5+card K |
| Full labels, including two live results and external labels | 18+card Λ |
| Full registers | 102×card R |
| Concrete Fin2 / Unit / Bool package | 7 stacks, 19 labels, 204 registers |

The owned-label subtype must have cardinality 16 without assuming Fintype Λ;
include a type-level specialization at Λ=Nat. For a finite ambient package,
derive counts from its actual carrier fields and Fintype instances. A separate
enumeration of an unrelated finite set is insufficient.

Every row is one outer TM2 activation, returns outer `some`, resets all owned

and suffixes; these are dirty-state facts, not clean-entry facts. The table's
tests are proof-side descriptions of the installed finite blocks.

Use every foreign Tag 2–15, both path Branches, both directions, absent/present
first and second source observations, and pending lengths 0, 1, 2. In particular,
the Unit temporary must hold the **peek after the pop**, not the earlier popped
value. A pending singleton completes; two old pending cells continue. Dirty
pending zero also completes on a Tag 0, and must not be excluded from the actual
table. Restore a foreign Tag before resetting the register that remembers it.

The fresh one-step experiment checked 11,136 combinations: 16 phases × 33 source
patterns × 3 pending lengths × 3 path patterns × 2 dirty-accumulator patterns,
then all 102 temporary tuples in each phase. It compared complete direct-table
and primitive-AST states, including frame/reset, marker conservation, potential
and strict natural-countdown descent. This finite support does not replace the
arbitrary-word one-step proofs.

## 3. Total dirty evaluation, rank, first return and physical space

Require a proof-only exact evaluator on an owned phase plus actual D. Its result
supplies the actual live result, complete final D and exact cost Q. Prove finite-block
one-step correspondence first, then actual `(next caller)^[Q]` endpoints. Never
install the proof-side evaluator, Q, tree recursion or whole-list equality in a
runtime callback. Q=0 outside owned control; Q>0 at every owned control.

For every actual configuration c and n≤Q(c), consume one shared reached state
with actual iterate, rank Q(c)−n, actual LocalStep closure, and
`n<Q(c) ↔ Owned reached.control`. Bind all frame/reset/space conclusions to that
same state. For n=0 the full state is c, including stale fields; for n>0 the
temporary tuple is zero. For an owned entry, at n=Q the result is live and no
caller body has run.
Nonowned starts have only the zero-step identity under this owned-prefix
contract. A later caller may enter an owned phase again; that does not extend
the original first-owned prefix.

Prove exact Q decrement at every owned transition, unconditional progress,
caller independence through the inclusive first return, ambient-program
agreement on all 16 bodies, and first-return uniqueness given that all strict
earlier labels were owned. Eventual reachability of a result alone cannot
characterize the original operation. Build actual Type-valued exact and bounded
`EvalsToInTime` records from the same endpoint execution, not from an existential
reachability proof.

Let L,Flen,Slen,Hlen,Plen be actual local lengths and W=3L+Flen+Slen+Hlen+Plen.
The proposed natural descent T is W+5 for seek/scanPrefix/scanScratch, W+4 for
start, W+6 for checkRight, Slen+Flen+2 for successful scratch restoration,
Slen+Hlen+Flen+3 for failed scratch restoration, Hlen+Flen+2 for dropping pending,
Flen+1 for saved restoration, and 0 outside owned control. Each actual owned
step must satisfy T(next)+1≤T(current); derive Q≤T. Clean entry gives
Q≤3L+Plen+5 and hence the retained conservative public 4L+Plen+12 bound. T is not
Q: the decrement can exceed 1. The operational exact rank is Q.

Physical cells are the unweighted sum of all five local stores plus every
protected stack. Prove equality with the actual dependent-index finite sum.
Debt is 1 in scanScratch left, checkRight, restoreScratch successRight/failureLeft;
debt is 2 in scanScratch right and restoreScratch successLeft/failureRight; it is 0
elsewhere. Every owned step preserves `tagCells+debt` exactly. Credit is the
actual source length during seek/scanPrefix/start/scanScratch/checkRight and 0
elsewhere. Potential=`cells+debt+credit` is nonincreasing at every owned step.
Thus every inclusive prefix is bounded by its actual initial potential. Clean
entry has potential 2L+Plen+U; retain U explicitly.

Two dirty separators prevent false strengthenings: empty
restoreScratch successLeft has 0 local cells but creates two source nodes in one
empty probe, so debt cannot be dropped; scanPrefix on X=[1], empty F/H creates
F=[1],H=[()] in one step, so physical cells plus debt without credit is not
monotone. The exact countdown and workspace potential are separate measures.

## 4. Arbitrary dirty transfers and their literal orientations

For scratch S=A++B, exactly |A| transfers retain the same restoreScratch mode,
leave S=B and put `A.reverse++X` on source. This includes B=[]: the marker
insertion still requires the next empty probe. All other local stores are
unchanged. Registers are original for A=[] and reset otherwise. An arbitrary
partial saved-prefix transfer has the same reversal law. Partial pending
drops preserve every other store and still need an empty probe after exhaustion.

Complete transfer expectations are:

| Entry phase | Exact Q | Final source | Other local state |
|---|---:|---|---|
| restoreScratch successLeft | Slen+Flen+2 | reverse F++[1,1]++reverse S++X | F/S empty; **H and P unchanged** |
| restoreScratch successRight | Slen+Flen+2 | reverse F++[1]++reverse S++X | F/S empty; **H and P unchanged** |
| restoreScratch failureLeft | Slen+Hlen+Flen+3 | reverse F++[1]++reverse S++X | F/S/H empty; P unchanged |
| restoreScratch failureRight | Slen+Hlen+Flen+3 | reverse F++[1,1]++reverse S++X | F/S/H empty; P unchanged |
| dropPending | Hlen+Flen+2 | reverse F++X | F/H empty; **S and P unchanged** |
| restorePrefix r | Flen+1 | reverse F++X | F empty; **S/H/P unchanged**; result r |

Concrete nonpalindromic case: X=[15,0],F=[12,3],S=[8,5],H=[(),()],P=[R,L].
SuccessLeft/SuccessRight return in 6 with sources
`[3,12,1,1,5,8,15,0]` / `[3,12,1,5,8,15,0]` and the old two pending cells.
FailureLeft/FailureRight return in 9 with those one-/two-marker sources and no
pending cells. DropPending returns in 6 with `[3,12,15,0]` and dirty scratch
`[8,5]`. Either restorePrefix result returns in 3 with that same source while
preserving both dirty scratch and pending. These are complete configurations,
not a statement that every phase called cleanup empties every auxiliary.

## 5. Scanner cases and the required pending premise

For a represented subtree t, source=`treeCode t++z`, pending=`()::outer`, and
arbitrary old accumulator A, exactly |treeCode t| activations leave accumulator
`(treeCode t).reverse++A` and pending outer. If outer is nonempty, remain in the
scanner. If outer is empty, scanPrefix goes to seek, scanScratch left goes to
checkRight, and scanScratch right goes to successful-right restoration with
source **1::z**; its source-node insertion occurs in the final scanner block.
The other scanner accumulator, saved context and path are preserved as the
particular table requires. The complete caller register and protected family are
preserved. All three owned temporary fields are reset, since a tree code is
nonempty and this scanner run therefore takes a positive number of steps. The
zero-step exception belongs to the general prefix theorem. Prove the tree
induction with arbitrary A and z; do not infer this theorem from a whole-word
parser call.

Pending-zero separator: from source `[1,0,0]` with no pending cells, scanning
Tag 1 creates one pending cell, and scanning the first Tag 0 empties it. At 2 the
prefix scanner has F=`[0,1]++oldF`, source=[0], pending=[], control seek. With
one initial pending cell it instead consumes all three Tags and ends at 3 with
F=`[0,0,1]++oldF`, source=[], pending=[]. The scratch scanners have the same
consumption split with their respective final controls/node insertion. A valid
source code does not remove the initial-one-slot premise.

Nonpalindromic right-scratch case: start with source
`[1,0,1,0,0,15,2]`,S=[8,5],F=[12,3],H=[()],P=[R,L]. At 5, control is
restoreScratch successRight, source=[1,15,2], scratch=[0,0,1,0,1,8,5],H=[].
The old F/P are untouched. This separates whole-code reversal, old-accumulator
placement and the same-block source-node insertion.

For arbitrary accepted prefixes w, use an actual continuing-scan relation:
Tag 1 increases slots; a **continuing** Tag 0 requires at least two old slots and
decreases them by one; epsilon leaves slots unchanged. If w is followed by EOF
or a foreign Tag, write Hlen for the pending count after w. Then:

- scanPrefix cleanup costs 2|w|+Hlen+Flen+3 and returns
  `reverse F++w++blocked`, preserving dirty scratch and path.
- scanScratch cleanup costs 2|w|+Hlen+Slen+Flen+4 and returns
  `reverse F++markers(direction)++reverse S++w++blocked`, clearing scratch and
  pending but preserving path. Failure markers are one for left and two for right.

The premise that all w transitions really continued is essential; an arbitrary
numerical slot count paired with an arbitrary syntactic w is insufficient.

## 6. Clean raw failure, malformed success and sharp families

Clean seek entry has saved/scratch/pending empty, but arbitrary raw source and
path, stale temporaries, caller and protected stores. Every failure restores
the **entire literal original source**, clears saved/scratch/pending, and keeps
the actual unconsumed path suffix. Success preserves source length, empties the
three auxiliary stores, and has consumed the path. Neither success nor source
length proves that the source was a tree code.

| Direction; source; path | First result/time | Final source; remaining path |
|---|---|---|
| either;[];[] | failure/4 | [];[] |
| left;[15,0];[L,R] | failure/3 | [15,0];[R] |
| right;[1,15,0];[] | failure/4 | identical source;[] |
| left;[1,15,0];[] | failure/7 | identical source;[] |
| right;[1,1,15,0];[] | failure/7 | identical source;[] |
| left;[1,0,15,2];[] | failure/8 | identical source;[] |
| left;[1,0,1,15];[] | **success/7** | [1,1,0,15];[] |
| either;[0];[L,R,L] | failure/3 | [0];[R,L] |

Both words in the success row fail even single-tree prefix recognition. This
local rotation routine is not an input validator. Each foreign-observation
position in the one-step table must also be covered universally for a:Tag with
a≠0 and a≠1, including restoration of an observed foreign second right-root
Tag in front of its untouched suffix.

For every n≥0, left root on raw 1^n with empty path returns failure in 3n+4.
At exactly 2n+2 it is in dropPending with source 1^n, pending ()^n, saved/scratch
empty. Its physical size is 2n+U, attaining the clean 2L+Plen+U bound. This includes
n=0: the intermediate at 2 is already dropPending with no local cells. Derive
the family from actual scanner/restoration transitions, not just numeric Q.

For every m≥0, right root on raw 1^(m+2) returns failure in 3m+7. At 2m+4 it is
dropPending with source 1^(m+2), pending ()^(m+1), no saved/scratch. Its cells are
2m+3+U=2L−1+U. Empty and singleton right-root words instead return in 4.

Also retain the path-stop family: for raw 1^n and path L^(n+k), k≥1, seek consumes
n successful ancestor heads and exactly one failing head, returns in 2n+3, restores
raw 1^n and leaves L^(k−1). It does not traverse the rest of an overlong position.
For path L^n, the separate root-at-EOF route takes 2n+4 and leaves empty path.

Dirty-entry separator: starting left seek on valid rightTwo code
`[1,0,1,0,0]` with one preexisting pending Unit returns failure in 14; clean entry
returns success in 7. Thus clean auxiliary premises are necessary for the clean
represented-entry theorem and cannot be silently removed or supplied by a name.

## 7. Represented trees, actual remaining path and separate clocks

Use actual treeCode and actual `applyMoveRun`; do not introduce a second encoding
as the semantic target. Fixtures are nil, one=node(nil,nil),
rightTwo=node(nil,one), leftTwo=node(one,nil), balancedThree=node(one,one),
leftContext=node(rightTwo,nil), and rightContext=node(one,rightTwo).

For arbitrary s, direction d, position p, old saved word F and untouched suffix z,
start seek d with source=`treeCode s++z`, saved F, scratch/pending empty and path p.
If actual applyMoveRun returns some t, final source is
`F.reverse++treeCode t++z`; on failure it is
`F.reverse++treeCode s++z`. All three auxiliary stores are empty; the protected
data/caller are exact. The extra restoration time for F is exactly |F|.

Define the remaining physical path recursively: [] stays[]; at nil with b::p,
return p; at a node follow the actual head and recurse on its tail/selected child.
In particular the failing branch at nil has already been popped. Successful
ancestor count j excludes that failed pop. The source operation does not inspect
the unvisited suffix of a missing-node path, and the machine must preserve it.

The exact clean represented machine clock C obeys:

- C(d,[],nil)=4; C(d,b::p,nil)=3.
- C(left,[],node A nil)=2|code A|+6.
- C(left,[],node A(node B C))=2|code A|+5.
- C(right,[],node nil C)=4.
- C(right,[],node(node A B)C)=2|code A|+4.
- C(d,L::p,node l r)=C(d,p,l)+2.
- C(d,R::p,node l r)=C(d,p,r)+2(1+|code l|).

The source tariff is independently fixed by Execution: root rotation success 4,
failure 2; empty applyAt path adds 1; each successful reconstructed ancestor adds 3,
each failed ancestor adds 2; nonempty path at nil costs 2 immediately.

## 9. Real package initialization and physical callers

The real finite package may choose source as both input and distinguished output,
with main=seek d and fixed initial caller state. Prove actual `Turing.initList`:
only source receives raw; saved/scratch/pending/path and protected stacks are
empty, temporaries zero. This is a **root** operation because no path is supplied.
Expose the same package.step for configurations installed by an actual earlier
handoff, with arbitrary source/path/protected contents. Do not claim free loading
of an arbitrary position or a total Boolean-output verifier from a live result.

Concrete initList separator: direction left, input leftContext code
`[1,1,0,1,0,0,0]`, initial caller false, all other stores empty. Genuine initList
performs a root failure in 16 and preserves that source. The same fixed program
with an actually installed path [L] succeeds in 9 to `[1,1,1,0,0,0,0]`. These are
different initial configurations; the second is not the package initializer.

All following continuations must be actual finite statements in the same ambient
program. Prove their own one-step equations and compose Type-valued timing with
the exact complete intermediate configuration. Transitivity uses the actual
second-plus-first budget order; no host reset/reinstallation is free.

1. **Sentinel/halt/none.** A result body pushes Tag 13 onto the protected Tag stack
   and halts in one activation. Minimal left-root success is live at 7, present
   halted at 8, outer none at 9. Nil with path [L,R,L] is live failure at 3 with
   remaining [R,L], present halted at 4, outer none at 5. Source/path/scratch and
   caller fields at the return persist through the caller except its one push.
2. **Different callers.** Tag 13 versus Tag 14 sentinel callers agree on every
   actual prefix through the original Q, then differ at Q+1. With the ordinary
   protected word their final Tag words are `[13,15,2,7,10,3]` and
   `[14,15,2,7,10,3]`. The owned-prefix independence theorem must stop at Q.
3. **Allocation.** Clean empty raw root returns failure at 4 with U cells, exactly
   its clean bound. A result body that pushes one protected Unit and returns to
   the same result has U+1 cells at 5 and U+2 at 6. The earlier bound remains true.
4. **Misleading result.** Minimal left-root success returns at 7; a caller goto
   failure reaches a later failure label at 8 without changing its successful
   source-connected first result. Also allow the symmetric fake-success route
   after actual failure. Eventual-label iff claims are false.
5. **External label.** Empty raw root gives live failure at 4; a result goto the
   separate external Unit label reaches it at 5; its push-Tag-13/halt body reaches a
   present halt at 6 and outer none at 7. This exercises the actual extra constructor.
6. **Consumed-path inverse.** Start leftContext=node(rightTwo,nil), direction
   left, physical path [L]. At 9 the live success source is node(leftTwo,nil), code
   `[1,1,1,0,0,0,0]`, and path is empty. A caller that only goto seek right takes 1;
   the new root-right operation takes 10 and reaches balancedThree at total 20,
   code `[1,1,0,0,1,0,0]`, which differs from the original. A caller that actually
   pushes Branch L then goto seek right also takes 1; the positioned inverse takes 8
   and at total 18 restores leftContext code `[1,1,0,1,0,0,0]`. This is a real
   new owned segment following the first return. Source `move.opposite` retains
   the original position; a consumed physical path does not reinstall itself.

## 10. Fresh finite support and remaining obligations

The fresh diagnostic checks 11,136 one-step states and 1,380 represented runs:
all 23 Unit tree shapes with at most four nodes × 15 positions of length at most 3
× 2 directions × 2 literal suffixes. Every represented run additionally starts
with dirty saved [12,3], so the exact extra restoration cost 2 and final prefix
[3,12] are checked. Source result and tariff come from a separate recursion
transcribing the inspected Execution equations; the expected machine time is
computed by the independent recursive C above. Every observed case matched.

Small additional results retain all 16 phases with dirty stores, the seven dirty
transfer modes, zero/one/two-slot scanner separators, malformed successes,
sharp families, complete minimal-root boundaries, initialization distinctions
and physical caller cases. The script asserts every owned transition resets
temporaries, preserves caller/protected data, conserves tags plus debt, decreases
the lexicographic termination measure and natural T, and does not increase the
workspace potential. These remain finite checks, not universal proofs.

The universal evaluator/iteration, exact first return, source correspondence,
all-prefix rank/frame/reset/space, typed timing and genuine finite-package
contracts are still to be authored and Lean-checked. The future Position client
must cover these fixed expectations through the producer's public contracts.
After that, Move→Position physical handoff, complete installed-program transport,
repeated stream/fuel execution, final equality/Boolean cleanup and halting,
quantitative TM2→TM1 simulation, formal NP and all canonical CTB obligations
remain separate required work. None is discharged by this preparation.

## 10. Actual physical space and the shared potential

Assume only Fintype K for summing protected physical cells. Let

`Cells(c) = Σ k : StackId K, |c.stk k|`

| Current control | D | E |
|---|---:|---:|
| M owned phase q | M.phaseDebt q | current source length |
| dispatch success d |2| current source length |
| dispatch failure |0| current source length |
| P owned phase q | P.phaseDebt q | P's actual phaseCredit q on its current data |
| any final/external label or none |0|0|

Use `Φ(c)=Cells(c)+D(c)+E(c)`.

During M, its own physical-cell-plus-delimiter debt is exactly conserved, its four protected Position stores and external ctx are literal, and |X| is unchanged. Hence Φ is exactly conserved by each M owned activation, including arrival at dispatch. This uses M's **success-result debt 2**, not debt 0 merely because M regards its result as external.

At success dispatch, all cells are unchanged and Φ falls by exactly 2: the old dispatch debt 2 disappears while P.seek supplies the same |X| credit. At failure dispatch, Φ falls by |X|. Neither step allocates storage. During P, its existing potential monotonicity extends by its literal protected certificate and moveReverse stores. Thus every whole owned activation has Φ(next)≤Φ(current).

For every actual n≤Q(c), the same reached state from the ranked prefix satisfies `Cells(reached)≤Φ(reached)≤Φ(c)`, alongside its rank/frame/reset facts. No promise extends to caller activations after Q.

For entry at M.start with B=[] the actual initial potential is

`|C| + |O| + 2|X| + |F| + |S| + |H| + U`.

This is valid even for dirty Position stores because the actual potential handles them. With F=S=H=O=[] it is `|C|+2|X|+U`. With arbitrary saved F and represented X=treeCode s++z retain |F| and the full literal X length, not merely the tree size.

There is also a useful sharper branchwise bound. On successful parse with p and rest, the M prefix is bounded by its actual initial cells

`A=|C|+|O|+|X|+|F|+|S|+|H|+U`,

while the Position prefix after dispatch is bounded by

The potential is not an exact remaining-time rank. Retain the inherited P marker/credit separators and an M-success debt separator. A callback that pushes protected cells after Q may exceed the bound; that does not invalidate the owned-prefix result.

# Independent cases for a proposed physical MoveParser → Position handoff

Status: complete independent case preparation, 2026-11-22; proposed mathematics
awaits reconciliation. This is new work for the
proposed next increment. It is not a recovered older proposal, a requirements
revision, an implementation release, a Lean build, or an original Standards/Spec
review. No repository owner is created or edited by this case preparation.

The expectations below are derived from the actual component definitions and
public contracts. The proposal author supplied only the carrier, mapping,
dispatch and initializer shape. Their expected tables and model have not been
read. Finite support, when completed, is separately identified and cannot prove
the universal statements proposed here.

## 1. Primary definitions and notation

All primary files are in `conaled/Applications/Resources/RotationCertificate/`:

| Source | Grounding used here |
|---|---|
| `Encoding.lean` | `Tag = Fin 16`; actual numeric tags; `treeCode`, `pathTags`, `moveCode`, lengths |
| `LinearParser.lean` | `parsePathRun`, `parseMoveRun`, their exact values, costs and prefix iff laws |
| `MoveParserMachine.lean` | complete `block`, all named one-step laws, `phaseResult`, `phaseSteps`, `run_source`, prefix/frame/debt/space and actual initializer |
| `PositionedRotationMachine.lean` | complete `block`, `advance_step`, arbitrary dirty phase endpoint/rank, represented and raw contracts, physical cell sum and genuine initializer |
| `Execution.lean` | actual `rotateRun`, `applyAtRun`, `applyMoveRun` and their source cost conventions |
| `FrontEndMachine.lean` | `Transport.statement`, `cfg`, `stepAux`, `iterate_owned`, `stackCells`; physical front-end stack alphabets |

Use `M` for MoveParserMachine, `P` for PositionedRotationMachine. Lists are
top-first. Branches are `L,R`; directions are `left,right`. Numeric tags are
`0=empty`, `1=node`, `6=rotateLeft`, `7=rotateRight`, `8=pathLeft`,
`9=pathRight`, `10=endMove`. A tag such as `15` is deliberately foreign.

The proposed physical data are

```
(C,V,O,X,F,S,H)
 certificate, moveReverse, path, source, saved, scratch, pending.
```

The first, fourth, fifth and sixth stores contain Tags; the second and third
contain Branches; the seventh contains Unit. `H` denotes the actual list, and
`|H|` its length. `ctx` is every protected store, `U` its actual cell sum when
its index type is finite. No finiteness of `ctx` is needed for a frame equality.

Registers are `((b,(a,u)),r)`, with the 102 possible triples
`b : Option Branch`, `a : Option Tag`, `u : Option Unit`, and arbitrary caller
register `r`. Define `tagReset` to clear only `a`; define `reset` to clear all
three temporary fields while preserving `r`.

Proposed labels are written `M.q`, `D.failure`, `D.left`, `D.right`, `P.q`, and
the three distinct final labels `parseFailure`, `rotationFailure`,
`rotationSuccess`; external caller labels remain separate. The three `D`
labels are **owned**, although each is a result label in the standalone M
component. P's result labels map directly to final rotation labels.

## 2. Physical architecture cases

The two component views must be complete stack equivalences, not projections
that silently discard stores. M's three local stores map to `(C,V,O)`; its
protected complement contains `(X,F,S,H)` and all `ctx`. P's five local stores
map to `(X,F,S,H,O)`; its protected complement contains `(C,V)` and all `ctx`.
The path has exactly one physical identity in both views.

M's local register type can be `Option Tag × ((Option Branch × Option Unit) × R)`.
The finite permutation

```
(a,((b,u),r)) ↦ ((b,(a,u)),r)
```

is an equivalence with the proposed global register type. M's reset therefore
becomes exactly `tagReset`, not P's `reset`. P's view is the identity register
view. The actual transport translates each finite primitive and callback; it
does not run a parser or manipulate a complete list in a callback.

The proposed three dispatch bodies all perform one `.load reset` and one
constant `.goto` within **one actual TM2 activation**:

| Entry label | Successor label | Stack effect | Register effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D.failure` | `parseFailure` | every store unchanged | `reset` |
| `D.left` | `P.seek left` | every store unchanged | `reset` |
| `D.right` | `P.seek right` | every store unchanged | `reset` |

Each case is universal over all seven dirty stores, protected contexts and all
102 temporary tuples. Even an arbitrary entry at a dispatch label with a
nonempty `V` preserves `V`. A dispatch does not check or repair data.

Carrier arithmetic follows the actual finite components: `7+16+3=26` owned
labels, three final labels, `29+|Λ|` total labels, `7+|K|` stack indices and
`102|R|` registers. For `K=Fin 2`, `Λ=Fin 2`, `R=Bool`, this is 9 stores,
31 labels and 204 register states. The 26 owned labels stay finite with
`Λ=Nat`; do not introduce a finite caller-label hypothesis into structural
execution, first-return or frame laws.

## 3. General principal-entry expectations

Principal entry is `M.start` with `V=[]`; `C`, old path `O`, all four tree
stores `(X,F,S,H)`, temporary fields, caller register and context are arbitrary.
Let `m=M.fullSteps C` and let `(parseMoveRun C).1` be the actual source parser
result.

### 3.1 Parser failure

If it is `none`, the first final result occurs at exactly `m+1`:

```
parseFailure, reset regs, (C,[],O,X,F,S,H), ctx.
```

At exactly `m`, the label is `D.failure`, all physical data already have that
same value, and registers are only `tagReset regs`. The next paid step clears
the remaining temporaries. The parser has restored the complete certificate;
every tree store and the old path are literally untouched. No tree cleanup is
part of this branch. In particular dirty saved, scratch and pending stacks
remain dirty at final parse failure.

The actual source tariff on this branch is `m+1`, by
`M.parseMoveRun_failure_cost`. Thus the composed machine's clock happens to
equal the source parser failure cost after charging the dispatch; that equality
does not extend to success.

### 3.2 Parser success and paid physical entry

If it is `some (⟨d,p⟩,rest)`, the source iff gives
`C=moveCode ⟨d,p⟩ ++ rest`. Then `m=2|p|+3` and:

| Time | Label | Physical data |
|---:|---|---|
| `m` | `D.d` | `(rest,[],p++O,X,F,S,H)` |
| `m+1` | `P.seek d` | exactly the same seven stores |
| `m+1+P.phaseSteps (seek d) D` | first final rotation result | the actual P phase endpoint, with `rest` and `V=[]` protected |

Here `D={source:=X,saved:=F,scratch:=S,pending:=H,path:=p++O}`. At time `m`
registers are `tagReset regs`; at every time from `m+1` through the first
final result they are `reset regs`. Direction comes from the actual parsed
direction label. No free transfer, path reconstruction, reinstall, extra seek,
or hidden cleanup occurs at the interface.

This exact endpoint law is valid for arbitrary dirty `D`. Semantic claims
about a represented tree or literal rollback use their actual additional
premises below; the arbitrary-state law itself has no such premises.

## 4. Dirty parser-phase expectations

These cases are necessary because principal entry's `V=[]` does not cover all
owned configurations. Let `v=|V|`, and write `Vʳ` for `V.reverse`.

| Actual M starting phase | Component endpoint | M clock; then paid dispatch |
|---|---|---|
| start, `C=[]` or foreign first direction | `D.failure`, same `C,V,O` | `1`; final parse failure at `2` |
| start, `C=directionTag d::raw`, path parser succeeds `(p,rest)` | `D.d`, `(rest,[],Vʳ++p++O)` | `2\|p\|+v+3`; then P at `+1` |
| start, direction accepted but path parser fails | `D.failure`, `(directionTag d :: (pathTags Vʳ ++ raw),[],O)` | `2 branchCount(raw)+v+3`; final at `+1` |
| scan d, succeeds `(p,rest)` | `D.d`, `(rest,[],Vʳ++p++O)` | `2\|p\|+v+2`; then P at `+1` |
| scan d, fails | `D.failure`, `(directionTag d :: (pathTags Vʳ ++ C),[],O)` | `2 branchCount(C)+v+2`; final at `+1` |
| emit d | `D.d`, `(C,[],Vʳ++O)` | `v+1`; then P at `+1` |
| undo d | `D.failure`, `(directionTag d :: (pathTags Vʳ ++ C),[],O)` | `v+1`; final at `+1` |

In every row M leaves `(X,F,S,H)` and `ctx` untouched. A direction-accepted
dirty failure **does not restore just the starting certificate**, because its
old reverse accumulator is materialized into that certificate. Immediate dirty
start failure instead preserves the accumulator. These are actual distinct
behaviors, not a contradiction or an admissible simplification.

Concrete separating inputs, all with old `O=[R]` and arbitrary fixed tree data:

| Input | Before dispatch | Final after the dispatch or remaining P run |
|---|---|---|
| `M.start`, `C=[15]`, `V=[R,L]` | at 1: `D.failure`, `C=[15]`, `V=[R,L]` | at 2: same stores, final parse failure |
| `M.start`, `C=[6,8,15]`, `V=[R,L]` | at 7: `D.failure`, `C=[6,8,9,8,15]`, `V=[]` | at 8: same stores, final parse failure |
| `M.start`, `C=[6,8,10,15]`, `V=[R,L]`, `X=[]`, other tree auxiliaries empty | at 7: `D.left`, `C=[15]`, path `[L,R,L,R]` | P entry at 8; final rotation failure at 11, path `[R,L,R]` |

## 5. Raw and represented outcomes

### 5.1 Clean raw tree interface

Specialize principal entry to `F=S=H=[]`, leaving raw `X`, old `O`, certificate
and registers arbitrary. Successful parsing enters P with physical path
`q=p++O`. By P's actual raw contracts, the first final rotation result has
saved/scratch/pending empty, an output `Y` of length `|X|`, and a residual path
that is a suffix of `q`. Rotation failure gives **literal** `Y=X`; rotation
success gives empty residual path. The certificate remains `rest` on both
rotation outcomes. A later rotation failure does not restore a previously
consumed certificate prefix.

Raw success is not a represented-tree validator. With empty path, the physical
left pattern is `X=1 :: (treeCode A ++ 1 :: z)`; right is
`X=1 :: 1 :: (treeCode A ++ z)`. Here `z` is any Tag word, including malformed
tails. At principal parsed empty position and old path empty, the exact
combined root clocks are `2|treeCode A|+9` left and
`2|treeCode A|+8` right. Arbitrary old saved `F`, with scratch/pending empty,
adds `|F|` and prepends `F.reverse` to the actual output.

### 5.2 Represented interface with arbitrary old path, saved prefix and suffix

Put `X=treeCode s++z`, `S=H=[]`, retain arbitrary `F`, and let parsing return
`(⟨d,p⟩,rest)`. Define `q=p++O` and
`a=(applyMoveRun ⟨d,q⟩ s).1`. The complete first endpoint must be:

```
label = rotationSuccess iff a is some, otherwise rotationFailure;
registers = reset regs;
certificate = rest; moveReverse = [];
source = F.reverse ++ treeCode (a.getD s) ++ z;
saved = []; scratch = []; pending = [];
path = P.remainingPath q s;
all ctx unchanged.
```

Exact machine time is

```
2|p| + 4 + P.representedClock d (p++O) s + |F|.
```

Source parser time is `3|p|+4`. The actual source application uses the extended
physical path `q`, not merely the parsed `p`. Its success tariff is `3|q|+5`.
Their sum is `3|p|+3|q|+9` on source success; this is an explicitly identified
sum of the two existing source costs, not a claim that a newly introduced
source program or full verifier has already been defined.

The final `source` length is `|F|+2*s.numNodes+1+|z|` on either outcome, by the
actual represented P contract. On success the returned tree has the same node
count, and the actual physical path is empty. Failure at nil after a path head
has been popped retains the tail after that failed head. In particular a
nonempty residual old path can remain.

Output converses must compare the complete represented output with the same
old `F`, cancel `F.reverse`, and use public tree-prefix injectivity to identify
both the returned tree and the suffix. Merely observing a success label after
an arbitrary caller step is not such a converse.

## 6. All-state first boundary, caller and reset obligations

A proposed exact all-state countdown can compose the actual component phase
endpoints: in an M phase, use M's exact remaining clock plus one dispatch step,
plus P's exact seek clock only if that actual M endpoint selects a direction.
At `D.failure` use 1; at `D.d` use `1+P.phaseSteps (seek d) D`; at a P phase use
its actual phase clock; at every nonowned label or present halt use 0.

The all-state endpoint must use the actual M endpoint stores before forming
P's data. Every actual owned successor should reduce this countdown by one.
Consequences to connect in the eventual client are exact iteration, strict
earlier ownership, first nonowned boundary uniqueness, caller independence
through the inclusive endpoint, and a Type-valued exact-time witness. Eventual
iteration alone cannot identify a first return under an arbitrary looping
caller.

The correct register prefix clause distinguishes stages:

- zero time retains all original fields;
- positive time still in the initial M segment, including its D endpoint,
  gives `tagReset regs`;
- after the paid dispatch, all fields are reset;
- an initial P phase resets all fields on its first step;
- an initially nonowned configuration has only the zero-length owned prefix.

Caller `r` and every protected stack are preserved on every owned step. M also
frames the four physical tree stores; P frames certificate and moveReverse.
An arbitrary caller can allocate, alter these stores/registers, jump to an
owned label, or emit a misleading result after the endpoint. Present live
result, present halt (`some cfg` with `l=none`), and outer `none` require
distinct observations and, under a halting caller, distinct paid steps.

## 7. Shared physical cells and a global potential

The actual sum over the seven disjoint stores is

```
B = |C|+|V|+|O|+|X|+|F|+|S|+|H|+U.
```

The path is counted once. Both complete transport maps preserve this sum by
`FrontEndMachine.Transport.stackCells`; adding both components' local sums
would count the shared path twice and omit neither component's complement in
a controlled way.

A sound proposed all-state potential is:

| Control | Potential |
|---|---|
| M phase q | `B+M.phaseDebt q+\|X\|` |
| D.left / D.right | `B+2+\|X\|` |
| D.failure | `B+\|X\|` |
| P phase q | `B+P.phaseDebt q+P.phaseCredit q D` |
| any final / other nonowned label | `B` |

M preserves its physical mass plus delimiter debt and leaves `X` unchanged.
Success dispatch preserves physical cells while dropping two debt units;
failure dispatch drops the reserved `|X|`. P's actual potential already
includes every cell in its protected complement. Therefore the proposed
global potential cannot increase along any owned activation. This is a paper
derivation from the actual component laws, still requiring its new formal
connection if the architecture is accepted.

Principal entry has potential
`|C|+2|X|+|F|+|S|+|H|+|O|+U`. This is an inclusive bound through its first
final result. On parser failure the tighter actual bound is the initial
physical `B`, with equality at the restored endpoint. On parser success with
parsed length `p`, a sharper two-stage bound is the maximum of the initial
physical sum and
`|rest|+2|X|+|F|+|S|+|H|+|p++O|+U`.

For clean tree auxiliaries a uniform time bound from P's actual countdown is
`3|C|+3|X|+|O|+3`; with arbitrary old tree auxiliaries add
`|F|+|S|+|H|`. This is a bound, not the exact clock or a source-operation
tariff. It is only claimed for principal M.start entry with empty reverse.

## 8. Genuine initializer and full integration boundary

For the proposed finite package, `k₀=certificate`, `k₁=source`, main=M.start,
and initial temporaries are reset. `Turing.initList machine C` installs **only
the certificate**. Every tree store, path, moveReverse and protected stack is
empty. It cannot preload a tree or reconstruct one for free.

Consequently a syntactically valid move can only reach rotation failure from
this genuine initializer: source is literally `[]`, which is not even the
code `[0]` of the empty tree. For parsed position `p`, its exact clock
is 8 when `|p|=0`, and `2|p|+7` when `|p|>0`; the residual path is `p.tail`. Parser
failure instead reaches parseFailure at `M.fullSteps C+1`.

The meaningful represented rotation theorem starts from an explicit installed
configuration with the physical tree and old path already present. It is
distinct from `initList`. Both contracts need actual typed package instances,
all stack-alphabet finiteness, and dimension checks rather than an equality
that merely renames the abstract transition function.

At the actual FrontEnd boundary, five compatible existing stores can be used:
certificateWord, sourceTree, treeReverse (saved), decodeReverse (scratch), and
pending. The proposed minimal handoff adds two Branch stores for moveReverse
and path. Target tree, fuel, other front-end stores and caller data must be in
the protected complement. Reuse requires complete physical maps and actual
owned installation agreement. It does not establish fuel inspection, EOF
routing, repeated execution, final cleanup, final Boolean halting, TM2→TM1
quantitative transfer, or the NP theorem. All of that programme remains open.

## 12. Caller, ambient and initializer separators

### 12.1 The first live result is the boundary of the claim

Instantiate either §9 success with a caller that halts on every final label.
At time Q the result is live; at Q+1 there is a **present halt configuration**
with all the same data and `l=none`; at Q+2 the option iteration is outer `none`.
The halt itself does not occur at Q. An initially present halt has Q=0 and
identity zero prefix; taking its next transition immediately yields outer none.

Use a second caller that pushes `true` on the first protected Bool stack,
flips the Boolean caller register, and goes to an external sentinel. Through
time Q all prefixes match the halting caller. At Q+1, physical cells have
increased by one and protected data/caller register have changed. Thus frame
and space claims must end at the inclusive first boundary. A universal bound
on all later caller computation is unsupported.

Use a third caller that, at parseFailure, merely goes to rotationSuccess.
The first parse failure in §9.3 remains at Q=8. At Q+1=9 there is a success
label with the same malformed certificate and dirty tree stores. This is an
explicit counterexample to identifying semantic success by an arbitrary later
occurrence of a result label. The first-return condition is material.

Installation agreement on all 26 owned labels is enough to transfer the
entire prefix to an ambient program; agreement at final/caller labels is not
required. Conversely, agreement only on M phases omits the three paid
dispatches and cannot establish the whole handoff.

success. With the same success-reentry caller, attempting a third call would

full verifier needs its separately specified EOF/fuel/final-result policy.

The complete endpoint equality includes B, O, certificate, tree stores and registers. It is stronger than a result-label equation and prevents an incorrect recurrence that loses the future P path.
